lesson.menu_desc: Reading a service agreement for a Houston water utility + although, even though, despite, and however -- 33 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 18 -- Contracts and Concessions
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Thiago Negrães | Lesson 18 -- Contracts and Concessions
lesson.grammar_point: although even though despite and however for concessions

listenings.text: Rachel here. I reviewed the draft service agreement for the East Side water utility. The monthly inspection is included, although emergency repairs are billed separately. The contractor must respond within four hours; however, the response time starts after the utility confirms access to the site. Despite the short response window, the agreement does not guarantee that every repair will be completed on the same day. Please read the scope and the exclusions before our call.

The agreement covers routine inspections and basic maintenance at both pumping stations. Although the contractor supplies standard tools, the utility provides replacement pumps and spare parts. Emergency work is available around the clock; however, a separate call-out fee applies after 6 p.m. The contractor is responsible for its own staff and safety equipment. Despite this support, the utility must keep the access road clear. The first review meeting is scheduled for next Thursday.

extra_audio.text: First, the utility and contractor review the service scope. Then, the utility confirms site access. After that, the contractor performs routine inspections. Emergency repairs are billed separately. Finally, both sides review the agreement next Thursday.

items.situation: The monthly inspection is included. Emergency repairs are separate. Join the ideas with although.
tips: Although inspections are included, emergency repairs are billed separately.

items.situation: A four-hour response is promised. The clock starts only after access is confirmed. Use however.
tips: Use a period or a semicolon before however.
The response time is four hours; however, it starts after access is confirmed.

items.situation: The fee is low. The service excludes replacement parts. Use despite.
tips: Despite is followed by a noun phrase.
Despite the low fee, replacement parts are excluded.

items.situation: Ask Rachel what the agreement covers and what it excludes.
The review is next Thursday. Tell the client when both sides are meeting.
tips: Use the present continuous for a fixed arrangement.
The review meeting is happening next Thursday.
